Definition: from G2644; exchange (figuratively, adjustment), i.e. restoration to (the divine) favor:--atonement, reconciliation(-ing).
BiblicalUsage: Reconciliation is the exchange that restores us to God's favour, and Paul says we have now received the atonement, and that the casting away of Israel was the reconciling of the world. God was in Christ reconciling the world unto Himself, not imputing their trespasses, and He has given us the ministry of reconciliation. The word is the whole story of the cross in one breath: enemies made friends by the blood of Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe reconciliation is the heart of the gospel, because I was God's enemy and He made peace at His own cost. I hold that I am now trusted with that same ministry, and I will carry the word of peace to everyone I meet.
